subject: Novapay security questionnaire: hosted API escrow, retention, and deletion details
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@novapay.com>

Cc: security@novapay.com

Subject: Novapay security questionnaire: hosted API escrow + TTL follow-ups

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Attached is our standard security questionnaire — a few items are marked as high priority for procurement and legal before we can go further:

1) Data escrow: we need an option for periodic tenant data export to an approved escrow vendor (in case of insolvency or platform exit). What export formats, encryption, and timelines can Redwood support?

2) Retention matrix: please confirm default retention windows for raw request bodies, request logs, analytics/aggregates, and backups. Do you have different windows for PII-tagged data?

3) Deletion attestations: if we request a tenant erasure, what is the end-to-end timeline (primary stores + backups), and can you provide an attestation?

4) Regional residency: we plan to process EU customer data for certain product flows. For Hosted API customers that require EU residency, do you provide region pinning for request data and logs?

I attached the questionnaire as well (Novapay_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Can you return a short Q&A by EOD PST? Procurement would like to capture any DPA or amendment needs in the initial SOW.

Thanks,

Sam Ellis
Head of Security & Third-Party Risk
Novapay

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Novapay security questionnaire: hosted API escrow + TTL follow-ups

Sam —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise answers; I attached a retention matrix and a small tenant-export sample for format reference. If you want, we can run through any of these on a 30-min call later today.

1) Data escrow / tenant export - Format: encrypted NDJSON (.ndjson) for request/response pairs plus a JSON file with tenant config (models used, routes, keys redacted). Exports include request timestamps, metadata, and any persisted artifacts.
- Encryption & handoff: exports are AES-256-GCM encrypted with a customer-provided public key or Redwood-generated key (customer retains private key).
- Timelines: on-demand full-tenant export target SLAs: 48 hours standard; 24 hours expedited with a support SOW. For scheduled periodic exports (e.g., monthly) we support automated encrypted archives delivered to an S3-compatible endpoint or escrow vendor (SFTP) with an agreed schedule.

2) Retention matrix (summary provided here; see attached PDF for full table)
- Raw request bodies (hosted API default): not persisted beyond request processing by default. For customers who enable "session retention" or store datasets for evaluation/analytics, default retention is 30 days unless overridden.
- Request logs (operational logs with non-payload metadata): retained by default for 30 days. Can be extended to 365 days for enterprise plans.
- Aggregated analytics & metrics: retained 90 days by default; longer windows available by contract.
- Backups & disaster recovery snapshots: backups are retained for 30 days in the primary region; immutable snapshot copies may be kept up to 90 days for operational recovery.
- PII handling: we do not automatically parse/retain PII separately; retention windows above apply. Customers can request targeted redaction or longer/shorter windows per dataset via the Console and via contract amendments.

3) Deletion attestations
- Primary stores: tenant purge action initiates synchronous deletion of tenant-configured persisted objects; target completion: 72 hours.
- Propagation to caches/b/kv stores: typically within 72 hours; small KV caches may clear within minutes.
- Backups & snapshots: removed from active backup sets and scheduled for deletion; final removal from immutable backup copies is targeted within 30 days.
- Attestation: we provide a signed erasure attestation (PDF) upon completion. For sensitive requests we can include a short technical summary of the purge workflow and logs showing object IDs removed.

4) Regional residency
- Hosted API: we support region pinning for request processing and storage (US, EU, APAC). For true EU-only residency we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment; however, for many customers we can configure the Hosted tenancy to process and store request artifacts only in EU zones and provide evidence of same. This requires an account-level configuration and SLA amendment.

Next steps: I attached the retention matrix (redwood_hosted_retention_matrix.pdf) and a small tenant_export_sample.ndjson to show structure. If escrow is required, we typically add a short escrow addendum to the DPA describing frequency, vendor, and storage responsibility.

I'll flag Ro (rohan) on the export mechanics and Marissa for DPA/Docusign routing — they can chime in below.

Best,

Thanks, Kimberly — that helps a lot. A few clarifying bullets from legal/security after a quick read:

• Escrow frequency: we prefer quarterly exports with a 30-day retention window in escrow. Is Redwood able to automate quarterly deliveries to an SFTP endpoint that the escrow vendor controls?
• Export completeness: does the NDJSON include full request/response payloads when a customer has enabled session retention? We need to ensure we’ll be able to rehydrate a working copy of the tenant in another vendor if necessary.
• Backup deletion attestations: is the 30-day window applied to all immutable snapshots, or are there circumstances where immutable copies persist longer (e.g., legal holds)?

Legal also asked for a sample erasure attestation template so they can confirm language before sign-off. Can you drop that into the Drive link you mentioned? Also, please indicate whether an escrow addendum is a standard DPA schedule item or an on-demand amendment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement wants to lock terms this week.

—Sam

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Novapay security questionnaire: hosted API escrow + TTL follow-ups

Sam — quick follow to close the loop and give legal the artifacts they asked for.

• Quarterly automated exports: yes — we can schedule encrypted quarterly exports to an SFTP endpoint managed by your escrow vendor. We can also deliver to an S3 bucket with Server-Side Encryption (SSE). Delivery is via encrypted transfer; credentials for the endpoint are customer-provided.

• Export completeness / rehydration: NDJSON export includes request/response pairs, metadata, model config references, and routing rules (secrets/redacted). For customers who enable session retention, exported payloads will include the full persisted content. Rehydration steps (documented) let an operator reconstruct a working tenant in a compatible runtime; the export sample attached demonstrates the field mapping. For enterprise deals we can provide a short rehydration runbook as an additional deliverable.

• Backups/legal holds: the 30-day target for immutable snapshot expiry is our baseline. Legal holds or regulatory obligations may require us to retain specific artifacts beyond that window; in those cases retention exceptions are documented and reported. We can include a clause in the DPA that codifies the standard 30-day snapshot expiry and the process for authorized holds.

• Erasure attestation: I uploaded a redacted attestation template and the retention matrix to the Drive link below. You should be able to download: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-Example-HostedAPI-Evidence

• Escrow addendum: typically handled as a DPA schedule item (on the DPA/contract) for recurring escrow deliveries; on-demand exports are available without amendment but recurring escrow requires a short schedule with vendor info.

Next steps: Marissa will prepare a DPA + escrow schedule draft and route via DocuSign. Ro will follow up with technical export options and the rehydration runbook. If procurement wants to review the DPA draft this afternoon I can trigger the DocuSign link.
